text: Which are true statements about terminal operations in a stream? (Choose all that apply.)

answers.text: At most one terminal operation can exist in a stream pipeline.
Terminal operations are a required part of the stream pipeline in order to get a result.
Terminal operations have Stream as the return type.
The referenced Stream may be used after the calling a terminal operation.

The 
peek()
method is an example of a terminal operation.

correct.description: Terminal operations are the final step in a stream pipeline[cite: 10]. Exactly one is required, because it triggers the execution of the entire stream pipeline. Therefore, options A and B are correct[cite: 11]. Options C and F are true of intermediate operations rather than terminal operations. Option E is never true[cite: 12]. Once a stream pipeline is run, the Stream is marked invalid[cite: 13].

text: Which terminal operations on the Stream class are reductions? (Choose all that apply.)

correct.description: Options D and E are incorrect because they are intermediate operations and not terminal operations[cite: 14]. While option F is a reduction, it is incorrect because it is available only on primitive streams such as IntStream[cite: 15]. Option C is incorrect because it is not a reduction—it does not look at each element in the stream[cite: 16].

Options C and D are incorrect because these methods do not take a Predicate parameter and do not return a boolean[cite: 17]. Options B and E are incorrect because they cause the code to run infinitely[cite: 18]. The stream has no way to know that a match won’t show up later[cite: 19]. Option A is correct because it is safe to return false as soon as one element passes through the stream that doesn’t match[cite: 20].

The sorted() method is used in a stream pipeline to return a sorted Stream[cite: 21]. A collector is needed to turn the stream back into a List. The collect() method takes the desired collector[cite: 22].

correct.description: The terminal operation must be right before the semicolon, which is line M. Remember that forEach() is a terminal operation while peek() is an intermediate operation[cite: 29]. This eliminates all but choices C, E, and F. Choice E is incorrect because there is no limit() operation, which means that the code would run infinitely[cite: 30]. Choice C is incorrect because filter() is called before limit(). No elements make it through the filter, so the code also runs infinitely[cite: 31]. Choice F is correct[cite: 32].
